Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your touchtone phone. If using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Chen, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Larson, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Patel, VP of Exploration; Tom Reilly, VP of Marketing; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to David Chen.

David Chen: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved operating expenses per BOE of $9.85, reflecting continued cost discipline. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on EBITDA, which rose 22% year-over-year. We are focused on environmental performance, with reportable spills down sharply. Further, we are working on lifting costs per BOE, now at record lows. We continue to adjust to market dynamics through prudent capital allocation priorities like dividends and buybacks. We are advancing capital expenditure breakdowns that came in under budget. Finally, we are taking steps with forward capital expenditure guidance to drive high returns.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Ramirez: Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.5 billion, up 22% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.2 billion, and net income was $850 million. We generated $1.1 billion in free cash flow and returned $600 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $4.5 billion in debt and $1.8 billion in cash.

Let me expand on some key metrics starting with our adjusted EBITDA, which reached $1.95 billion for the quarter, a robust 22% increase year-over-year from the prior period. On a trailing twelve-month basis, it's at $7.5 billion, up 18%. This highlights the resilience of our integrated upstream, midstream, and refining operations despite OPEC+ cuts and Middle East tensions. Realized upstream prices averaged $78.50 per BOE, up 15%, with WTI at $82, Brent at $86, and better differentials for our Gulf assets thanks to Matterhorn Express. Natural gas hit $3.25 per MMBtu on LNG demand. Production grew 8% to 425,000 BOE per day, led by Permian output up 12% to 220,000 BOE/d via cube developments with 12,000-foot laterals and AI completion tools boosting EURs 15% to 1.2 MBOE per 10,000 feet. Bakken added from acquisitions, Eagle Ford from CO2 EOR. Costs helped too: LOE at $12.50 per BOE down 7% with Smart Wells IoT cutting downtime 18%; gathering flat at $4.20 via midstream JV; G&A down 5% post-divestitures. Refining cracks at $28 per barrel on 94% utilization. U.S. onshore drove 65% growth, Gulf 20%, Guyana stake ramping to 25,000 BOE/d net. This funds 40% drilling, 30% debt paydown to 1.1x leverage, 30% returns with $0.75 dividend and $1 billion buyback.

Turning to operating expenses per BOE, our company-wide figure was $9.85, a 4% sequential drop from Q2's $10.25 and 12% year-over-year from $11.20, the lowest since 2019 pre-pandemic. Trailing twelve months at $10.15, top quartile vs. Permian peers per Enverus. Over three years, from $13.50 peak in Q3 2021 amid inflation and shortages, down to $12.40 in 2022, $11.50 TTM 2023 on low gas, now 22% off peak outperforming peers. Components: LOE $6.20 down 14% on fewer ESP failures; workovers $2.15 down 20% with 30% less downtime; gathering $1.50 flat via midstream stake; other $1.15 up slightly. Permian at $7.80 best-in-class like EOG; Bakken $11.20; GoM $14.50 offset by high netbacks. Learning curve from 10 million lateral feet drilled, plus easing inflation. Strategies include $150 million YTD investment yielding 3.5x ROI: Delfi platform AI for 25% fewer ESP pulls saving $0.45/BOE, digital twins for paraffin; longer laterals and cube devs spreading costs, 15% less water disposal; take-or-pay sand contracts, midstream ownership, diesel hedges; labor down to 0.8 FTE/BOE with drones; Permian electrification, Bakken PCP pumps, GoM ROVs; data-led workovers boosting runtime to 94%. Guide TTM $9.50-$10.00, Permian sub-$7.50 with $200 million tech next year.

Closely related, our lifting costs per BOE—or LOE—averaged $9.85 for the year to date, down 12% from 2023's $11.20 and 28% from 2020's $13.65, with Q3 at $9.42, a record. Onshore 72% of production at $7.80 down 15%, Permian $6.50 post-Pioneer synergies, Eagle Ford $8.20. Offshore $14.25 down 7%, GoM $16.80 deepwater, shelf $11.20, Nigeria $13.40. Five-year CAGR -7.9% consolidated, Permian -6.8%, GoM -6.2%. $450 million savings since 2021 Efficiency 2.0, $120 million this year. Levers: ApexAI on 85% wells cutting downtime 22% to 3.3%, ESP to gas-lift hybrids extending run times; electrification slashing diesel $0.45/BOE; supply chain contracts 10-15% below peaks, vendor consolidation; 850 workovers at $52k/well; Permian scale to $28 breakeven. On track for $9.20 in 2025 with CCUS upside.

On capital allocation, with $3.1 billion levered FCF YTD at $82 Brent, priorities are dividends first—up 10% to $0.85 quarterly, $3.40 annual, 3.8% yield, 42% payout, $2.8 billion YTD, covered at $50 WTI; buybacks $1.2 billion this quarter at $112/share, $3.5 billion YTD vs. $8 billion auth, refresh $5 billion, metrics-driven below 8x EV/EBITDA; reinvestment $6.5 billion 2025 capex at 15% IRR min—$2.8 billion Permian cubes, Guyana Stabroek, North Sea Buzzard, Qatar LNG, Permian CCUS, Gulf refining. 50-60% FCF to returns, guide $18-20 billion 2025 FCF.

For capex breakdown YTD through Q3: $1.95 billion vs. $2.1 billion budget, $150 million under. Drilling 45% at $890 million vs. $945 million: 22 rigs, 12% faster to 18 days/well, Permian $620 million under on pad efficiencies, cost/foot $650 down 9%. Completion 35% $720 vs. $735: 85 wells, 22 stages/day simul-fracs, AI designs boosting EUR 5-7%. Facilities 20% $340 vs. $420: Permian gathering $120 million ahead, water recycling. Savings to higher returns.

Forward capex guidance 2025 $2.8-3.0 billion midpoint up 15%, 65% Permian 45 rigs 1,800 BOE/d IP at 25-30% IRR $65 WTI, 12k ft laterals electric fracs; GoM $560-600 million Lucius/Winterfell 22% IRR; int'l/expl $280-300 million Guyana/Stabroek, Namibia; tech/sustain $140-150 million AI/CCUS/electrification 22-27% avg IRR, FCF $1.2 billion at $70 WTI.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Larson for an operational update.

Mike Larson: Thank you, John. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 425,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Delaware Cube Pad 1 online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives, including AI predictive maintenance and optimized artificial lift across our assets.

Now I will turn it over to Lisa Patel for an update on our exploration activities.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Delaware Basin and are planning to drill six exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio, with high-impact prospects targeting Wolfcamp and Bone Spring plays.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Tom Reilly to discuss our marketing strategy.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Lisa. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for Permian crude in the Gulf Coast market, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of these low-carbon barrels is significant, supporting premium pricing in LNG-linked deals.

I will now turn it over to Elena Vasquez to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Tom. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. Turning to spills, incidents, and remediation, 2024 has been our safest year, with just seven reportable spills, down 53% from 2022 and 78% from 2021. Total volume 0.42 barrels, intensity 0.001 bbls/mmBOE, far below API average and Chevron's. All Tier 1, zero offshore. Permian three produced water releases 0.18 bbls down 60% via acoustic sensors on 85% wells; midstream two seeps 0.15 bbls; downstream two leaks 0.09 bbls. TRIR 0.12 vs. industry 0.25. Prevention via 450 ILI pig runs mitigating 1,200 anomalies, AI SCADA, offshore DAS 99.9% accuracy. Remediation: all within 14 days, 98.7% recovery, $2.4 million cost down 40%. Bioremediation 60%, dispersants, 15,000 shrubs planted. $450 million 2024 capex for drones, hull conversions, saving $18 million insurance. 2025 under 0.3 bbls with Digital Twin rollout, hydrogen flaring pilots. This de-risks ops, aids green bonds, AA ESG score.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Joe Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Joe Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the operating expenses per BOE trend analysis and cost management strategies?

David Chen: Good question, Joe. As John detailed, our $9.85 opex per BOE marks multi-year progress through digitalization like Delfi AI, supply chain locks, and regional optimizations, positioning us top quartile. This supports sustained FCF at current prices.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mary Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mary Johnson: Good morning. What are your expectations for EBITDA YoY change and key drivers going forward?

John Ramirez: Thanks, Mary. We see continued strength from volume growth in Permian and Guyana, price realizations above $78/BOE, and cost controls holding LOE sub-$10. Q4 guide $2.0-2.2 billion assuming $80-85 WTI, with refining tailwinds.

Operator: Our next question comes from Alex Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Kim: Could you please provide more color on lifting costs per BOE trends and reduction initiatives?

Mike Larson: Absolutely, Alex. Our $9.42 Q3 low reflects ApexAI downtime cuts, lift optimizations, and electrification, with Permian leading at $6.50. Expect $9.20 in 2025 as tech scales.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Lee with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Rachel Lee: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Lisa Patel: Great point, Rachel. Positive seismic in Delaware confirms Tier 1 inventory extension, allowing us to high-grade D&C to 60%+ IRR locations, balancing growth with returns while derisking via farm-downs.

Operator: Our next question comes from Brian Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Brian Patel: What is the outlook for the new product in the coming years?

Tom Reilly: Brian, our low-carbon Permian crude outlook is bright, with expanding Gulf demand and LNG offtake, targeting 20% volume growth by 2026 at premiums via CCUS integration.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Elena Vasquez: Sure, Laura. Beyond spills under 0.3 bbls, we're targeting 20% TRIR cut with Digital Twins, Scope 1+2 net-zero by 2035, 2 MMtpa CCUS by 2027, leveraging IRA incentives for hydrogen and electrification.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to David Chen for closing remarks.

David Chen: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
